items.title: Replace the `RemoteWriteQueue` and `WAL` with the exporterhelper queue (sending_queue) in Prometheusremotewriteexporter
items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/prometheusremotewrite

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The Prometheusremotewriteexporter currently does not use the more general `sending_queue` in the exporterhelper (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/README.md) developed by the otel collector community for configuring in-memory or persistent queuing. Instead, it has a separate mechanism for setting up a persistent queue using the `WAL` config, which currently has some bugs (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/15277). It also needs a different setting to configure parameters like queue size etc. in the `RemoteWriteQueue` config. It will instead be much easier to instead replace these two configs in the exporter by the exporterhelper sending_queue as it provides all these features as part of a single `sending_queue` config, and will also make the Prometheusremotewriteexporter settings conform with most other exporters which are using the exporterhelper queue.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I propose that we replace the `RemoteWriteQueue` and `WAL` in the Prometheusremotewriteexporter config with `exporterhelper.QueueSettings` (`sending_queue`) so as to make the config better conform with most other exporters which are using the `sending_queue`. This will also remove the effort of separately maintaining the queuing related code for Prometheusremotewriteexporter, as the exporterhelper queue is maintained by the wider otel collector community.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

### Additional context

I have made changes to the Prometheusremotewriteexporter code locally to use the exporterhelper queue instead of the  `RemoteWriteQueue` and `WAL` and tested it. The changes do not require extensive code changes as `exporterhelper.QueueSettings` imports all the necessary code for the exporterhelper queue. The only changes needed would be in the `config.go` file to add some validations for the queue and some changes would be needed in the `exporter.go` file to remove the WAL related and RemoteWriteQueue related code, which should be straightforward.

items.title: exporting logs when network is down
items.body: ### Component(s) exporter/googlecloud ### Describe the issue you're reporting I have read through #31033 which talks about metrics, and #34957 which talks about traces. I want to confirm that the same issue exists regarding logs, and that there's no way to solve it with configuration. My use case is that I want to collect system logs and export them to GCP logging. It works fine when the network is up, but as soon as the network goes down, all logs are dropped. It would however be very useful to have these logs to diagnose connectivity issues. Basic config example: ``` receivers: journald: storage: file_storage priority: info start_at: beginning exporters: googlecloud: log: default_log_name: otel-systemd-journal ``` As I understand it, the retry functionality of OpenTelemetry has been disabled, and so none of the functionality provided by `sending_queue` helps. We are forced to rely on the retry logic of the Google client library, which I think suggests that any outage lasting longer than 60 seconds will cause permanent loss of data https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-go/blob/5bfee69e5e6b46c99fb04df2c7f6de560abe0655/logging/apiv2/logging_client.go#L84-L97 As an aside I see no evidence that retry in the client library actually works. The first image shows log messages captured by OpenTelemetry during a network outage. Note the large gap in entries. The second shows log entries captured by our custom logging app (which I was hoping to retire). The first log message reporting dropped entries appears only 1.3 seconds after the first log entry which was not uploaded. I very much hope I've missed something basic here, but please confirm. ### Tip [React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).

items.title: [pkg/stanza/fileconsumer] graceful shutdown under back pressure checkpoints a batch that was never enqueued (synchronous emitter, full persistent queue)
items.body:
### Component(s)

pkg/stanza, receiver/filelog

### What happened?

**Description**

With the `stanza.synchronousLogEmitter` feature gate and an exporter `sending_queue` (persistent storage, `block_on_overflow: true`) that is full, a filelog receiver that is reading a batch blocks in `ConsumeLogs`. On a graceful shutdown the batch is checkpointed as read although it was never enqueued, so it is skipped after the restart.

Code path (v0.159.0, unchanged on `main` and in the release notes up to v0.163.0):

1. `pkg/stanza/fileconsumer/file.go` `Manager.Stop()`: `m.cancel()` → `m.wg.Wait()` → `checkpoint.Save(context.Background(), …)` — the reader context is cancelled while readers are still emitting, and the offsets are saved afterwards.
2. The blocked enqueue into the full persistent queue returns `context canceled` (`ConsumeLogs() failed`).
3. `pkg/stanza/operator/helper/emitter.go` `SynchronousLogEmitter`: `consumerFunc func(context.Context, []*entry.Entry)` has no error result, so `Process`/`ProcessBatch` return `nil`.
4. `pkg/stanza/fileconsumer/internal/reader/reader.go` `readContents`: an emit error is only logged (`failed to emit token`); `r.Offset = s.Pos()` is set anyway.
5. `Stop()` persists that offset; after the restart the batch is skipped.

`block_on_overflow` / `wait_for_result` only change where the producer waits; there is no option that keeps the checkpoint on a failed emit.

**Steps to Reproduce**

- filelog receiver with `storage` (file_storage), `stanza.synchronousLogEmitter` enabled, exporter with persistent `sending_queue`, `block_on_overflow: true`, small queue (e.g. 400 kB).
- Make the exporter endpoint unreachable, write 6000 lines into a watched file until the queue is full.
- `systemctl stop` the collector (SIGTERM), start it again, make the endpoint reachable.

**Expected Result**

All 6000 lines arrive (an emit that did not succeed must not advance the offset; `Stop` should let in-flight emits finish or abort them without checkpointing their offsets).

**Actual Result**

5900 of 6000 lines arrive — exactly one read batch (100 lines) is lost. With SIGKILL instead of SIGTERM nothing is lost (offsets are not saved on the cancelled path).

### Collector version

v0.159.0 (otelcol-contrib), code unchanged on `main`

### Environment information

Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, otelcol-contrib linux binary, systemd service.

### Suggested fix

Propagate the consumer error through the synchronous emitter (`consumerFunc` returning `error`), keep `r.Offset` unchanged when the emit fails, and do not checkpoint offsets of emits that were aborted by `Stop()`.

items.title: [exporter/clickhouse] Schema detection error is cached as "feature absent", permanently dropping *AttributesKeys columns
items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/clickhouse

### What happened?

## Description

The ClickHouse exporter treats SpanAttributesKeys / ResourceAttributesKeys as optional "feature columns." At startup, (*tracesJSONExporter).start calls detectSchemaFeatures() → internal.GetTableColumns(), which runs DESC TABLE, sets an AttributeKeys flag only if those columns are present, then renders the INSERT statement once and caches the result for the lifetime of the process (renderInsertTracesJSONSQL).

Since #46286, a detection error is non-fatal. It is logged and ignored. That prevents the collector from crashlooping when ClickHouse is temporarily unavailable or overloaded, but it introduced a new problem. It treats all schema detection errors as "feature absent", even if the ClickHouse schema actually does contain the *AttributesKeys columns. If detectSchemaFeatures() happens to run during a transient ClickHouse outage (connection refused, transient network error, TOO_MANY_SIMULTANEOUS_QUERIES, etc.), the exporter caches an INSERT that omits the keys columns and then writes every subsequent row without them, even after ClickHouse becomes healthy again. That incorrect detection is cached permanently.

The consequence is a silent, persistent degradation. The collector reports healthy throughout and SpanAttributes (the nested JSON) stays fully populated. But, the flat *AttributesKeys index arrays are left empty, which breaks anything downstream that relies on them.

#46286 addresses recovery from connection errors by saying "let the sending queue / failover handle connection errors". But, that only covers the data path. The sending queue retries inserts using the already-degraded cached statement, but it never re-evaluates the feature decision, so it never recognizes the cached INSERT is wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the clickhouseexporter JSON traces path against a ClickHouse table that does have the SpanAttributesKeys / ResourceAttributesKeys columns, with create_schema: false.
2. Make ClickHouse briefly unreachable at the moment the collector starts (e.g. restart the collector while ClickHouse is bouncing, or point it at a CH that is mid-restart). The window only needs to cover the exporter's Start → DESC TABLE call.
3. Observe the collector log the (non-fatal) detection failure, e.g.:
    ```
    level:   error
    message: schema detection failed
    caller:  clickhouseexporter@v0.150.0/exporter_traces_json.go:69
    error:   get table columns: dial tcp <ch>:9440: connect: connection refused
    ```
4. Let ClickHouse come back healthy. The collector does not restart or re-detect.
5. Inspect the actual INSERT the exporter issues (e.g. ClickHouse system.query_log, extractAll(query,'(\w*AttributesKeys)')).

A side-by-side confirms the behavior is purely a function of CH availability at startup:
* Collector that started while CH was up → INSERT includes ['ResourceAttributesKeys','SpanAttributesKeys'].
* Collector that started during the CH blip → INSERT omits them ([]), and stays that way.

## Expected Result

A detection error should be treated as "schema unknown," not "feature absent." The exporter should not permanently cache a degraded INSERT based on a failed probe. Specifically:

* Keep the non-fatal start behavior from #46286 (do not regress #46285 by reverting to fatal).
* Only a successful DESC TABLE that returns the column set should drive the cached decision: keys columns present → enable; keys columns genuinely absent → degrade. Any error, including "connection refused" or "table not found" should be "schema unknown," not "feature absent." An unavailable ClickHouse or missing table says nothing about the schema the table will have once it appears, so the exporter must not infer column absence from it. It should defer and re-detect with backoff. (Note #46285's own repro, TOO_MANY_SIMULTANEOUS_QUERIES, is likewise a retryable "unknown.")
* On detection error, defer and re-detect — lazily before the first batch and/or periodically with backoff — until a definitive read succeeds.

Once ClickHouse is healthy, the exporter should write the keys columns without any operator intervention.

## Actual Result

A transient ClickHouse unavailability at collector startup causes the exporter to silently and permanently disable the *AttributesKeys columns for the life of the process. The decision is cached after a single failed DESC TABLE and is never re-evaluated, even after ClickHouse recovers. The collector reports healthy, no error recurs, and the only externally visible symptom is that newly-written rows have empty SpanAttributesKeys / ResourceAttributesKeys while the JSON SpanAttributes stays fully populated. Recovery currently requires manually restarting the collector at a time when ClickHouse is reachable.


### Collector version

v0.150.1. Affects v0.147.0+. (The enabling change is PR #46286, first shipped in 0.147.0.)

### Environment information




### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

```yaml
(The otel_traces table pre-exists with SpanAttributesKeys and ResourceAttributesKeys columns present.)


exporters:
  clickhouse:
    async_insert: false
    compress: lz4
	create_schema: false     # schema managed externally; detection is non-fatal
	database: otel_traces
	endpoint: tcp://<clickhouse>:9440?secure=true
	json: true               # JSON traces path — exporter_traces_json.go
    metrics_table_name: otel_metrics
    password: ${env:CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD}
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 5s
      max_elapsed_time: 30m
      max_interval: 30s
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      num_consumers: 2
      queue_size: 1000
    timeout: 30s
    traces_table_name: otel_traces
    username: <user>
```

### Log output

```shell
level:   error
ts:      2026-06-02T22:29:43.454Z
message: schema detection failed
caller:  clickhouseexporter@v0.150.0/exporter_traces_json.go:69
error:   get table columns: dial tcp <clickhouse>:9440: connect: connection refused
```

### Additional context

_No response_

### Tip

<sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

items.title: Bug: Buffered logs are lost after restart when fsync: false
items.body:
## Description

When using the persistent sending queue with `fsync: false`, logs buffered while the exporter is unable to reach its destination are lost if the Collector is restarted before connectivity is restored.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the file storage extension with:

   ```yaml
   fsync: false
   ```
2. Start the Collector and verify logs are being exported.
3. Simulate the exporter being offline by making DNS lookups for the AWS S3 endpoints return `NXDOMAIN`.
4. Continue sending logs for approximately one hour.
5. Restart the Collector while the exporter is still offline.
6. Restore connectivity.

## Expected Result

The buffered logs should be retained by the persistent queue and exported once connectivity is restored.

## Actual Result

After the Collector restarts, all logs received between the start of the outage and the restart are lost. Only logs received after the restart are exported.

## Notes

The outage was simulated by blocking DNS resolution for the AWS S3 endpoints (returning `NXDOMAIN`). It is unclear whether this behavior is expected when `fsync: false`, but losing the entire buffered backlog after a restart was unexpected.



### Collector version

0.151.0


### Otel Config Example

```

    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

processors:

        value: ${DEVICE_SERIAL_NUMBER}

    attributes:
      - key: "boot.id"
        action: "upsert"
        value: ${BOOT_ID}
  batch:
    timeout: 10s

exporters:

    path: /mnt/logs/otel-collector-metrics/file/metrics.log
    rotation:
      max_megabytes: 100
      max_days: 7
      max_backups: 3

    s3uploader:
      region: ${AWS_REGION}

      s3_partition_format: "%Y/%m/%d/%H/%M"
      compression: gzip

    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      storage: file_storage/metrics
      queue_size: 5000
      block_on_overflow: true
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 5s
      max_elapsed_time: 0
      multiplier: 1.5

  file/events:
    path: /mnt/logs/otel-collector-events/file/events.log
    format: json
    rotation:
      max_megabytes: 100

      s3_partition_format: "%Y/%m/%d/%H/%M"
      compression: gzip
      file_prefix: events
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      storage: file_storage/events
      queue_size: 5000
      block_on_overflow: true
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 5s
      max_elapsed_time: 0
      multiplier: 1.5

  file_storage/metrics:
    directory: /mnt/logs/otel-collector-metrics/buffer
    timeout: 10s
    compaction:
      directory: /mnt/logs/otel-collector-metrics/buffer
      on_rebound: true
      rebound_needed_threshold_mib: 4096
  file_storage/events:
    directory: /mnt/logs/otel-collector-events/buffer
    timeout: 10s
    compaction:
      directory: /mnt/logs/otel-collector-events/buffer
      on_rebound: true
      rebound_needed_threshold_mib: 4096

service:
  
  # Extensions enabled in config-service.yaml
  
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource/device_identity, resource/boot_identity, batch]
      exporters: [file/metrics, awss3/metrics]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource/device_identity, resource/boot_identity, batch]
      exporters: [file/events, awss3/events]

items.title: Enhance Kafka exporter to respect max message size

labels.name: never stale
labels.description: Issues marked with this label will be never staled and automatically removed

items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/kafka

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The exporter has a config option `MaxMessageBytes` but it itself does not respect it and attempts to send a full serialized payload to the Kafka driver which may reject it based on this setting.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Most payloads can be safely split into chunks of "safe" size that will be accepted by the Kafka driver. For example, in Jaeger integration tests there is a test that writes a trace with 10k spans, which is 3Mb in size when serialized as JSON. The trace can be trivially split into multiple messages that would fit in the default 1Mb size limit.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

### Additional context

https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/6437#issuecomment-2564811186

items.title: Logs are dropped when Elasticsearch is down even with persistent storage and retry enabled
items.body:
### Component(s)

Elasticsearch exporter

### What happened?

## Description

Logs are dropped immediately when Elasticsearch is down, even with persistent storage and retry enabled in OTel Collector v0.144.0. Goal is to store logs and retry exporting once ES is back.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure OTel Collector with sending_queue using file_storage and retry enabled.
2. Stop Elasticsearch service.
3. Send logs to the collector.

## Expected Result

Logs should be stored in persistent storage and retried until Elasticsearch is back.

## Actual Result
Logs are dropped immediately with errors like:

```
failed to execute the request: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9200: connect: connection refused
Exporting failed. Dropping data.
```

### Collector version

otelcol-contrib version 0.144.0

### Environment information

## Environment
OS: (e.g., "Ubuntu 20.04")
Compiler(if manually compiled): (e.g., "go 14.2")


### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

```yaml

    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317

        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

items.title: missing data with persistent queues enabled during network outages
items.body: ### Component(s) extension/storage/filestorage ### What happened? **Describe the bug** Observed a consistency issue in gateway-collector when the otlphttp exporter queue uses file_storage for persistent queue storage. When **gateway-collector egress** is blocked with a network policy, **gateway-collector** experiences a network outage for approximately **3 days and 16 hours**. During recovery the data missing from the **first 4 hours** of the outage window. This has been reproduced multiple times with different window outages, and the missing data always appears at the beginning of the network connectivity issue. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Configure **gateway-collector** with persistent queue storage using `sending_queue.storage: file_storage/telemetry-retention`. 2. Apply a network policy that blocks **gateway-collector egress**. 3. Create a network outage 4. Restore connectivity. 5. Review the exported telemetry and compare the recovered data against the outage duration. **What did you expect to see?** All telemetry buffered during the outage should be retained and exported after connectivity is restored, including data from the start of the outage. **What did you see instead?** The **first 4 hours** of telemetry are consistently missing. The remaining telemetry for the rest of the outage period appears to be preserved. ### Collector version Contrib 0.145.0 ### Environment information ## Environment OS: (e.g., "Ubuntu 20.04") Compiler(if manually compiled): (e.g., "go 14.2") ### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration ```yaml otlphttp: endpoint: tls: insecure: false insecure_skip_verify: false sending_queue: block_on_overflow: true queue_size: 15000 storage: file_storage/telemetry-retention wait_for_result: true retry_on_failure: enabled: true initial_interval: 5s max_elapsed_time: 10m max_interval: 30s batch: send_batch_max_size: 1000 send_batch_size: 500 timeout: 10s extensions: file_storage/telemetry-retention: compaction: check_interval: 1m cleanup_on_start: true directory: on_rebound: true on_start: true create_directory: true directory: timeout: 10s service: extensions: - file_storage/telemetry-retention telemetry: logs: level: info pipelines: logs/pod: receivers: [otlp] processors: [memory_limiter, k8sattributes, batch] exporters: [otlphttp] ``` ### Log output ```shell ``` ### Additional context Am I missing something or my setup is incorrect? ### Tip [React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).

items.title: [exporter/azureblob] Add sending_queue and timeout support
items.body:
**Component(s):** exporter/azureblob

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The azureblobexporter does not support `sending_queue` or `timeout` configuration. Without `sending_queue`, there is no persistent storage-backed queue for buffering exports during transient failures — data can be lost if the exporter process restarts during a failure window. Without `timeout`, there is no way to configure how long the exporter waits for a blob upload to complete.

The `awss3exporter` in this same repository already supports both via `exporterhelper.QueueBatchConfig` and `exporterhelper.TimeoutConfig`. The azureblobexporter only supports `retry_on_failure` today.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add `sending_queue` and `timeout` support to the azureblobexporter.

This enables configuration like:

```yaml
azure_blob:
  url: "https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/"
  sending_queue:
    enabled: true
    num_consumers: 10
    queue_size: 1000
    storage: file_storage
  timeout: 30s
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Using a batch processor in the pipeline provides some batching, but does not provide persistent storage-backed queuing at the exporter level. The exporterhelper queue is the standard approach in the collector ecosystem.

items.title: [processor/k8sattributes] Steady memory growth from Go map bucket retention in high-churn clusters
items.body:
## Description

The `k8sattributes` processor steadily leaks memory in clusters with high pod churn. `otelcol_process_runtime_heap_alloc_bytes` grows linearly (~500 MB/day) with no plateau, eventually causing OOM kills.

The `c.Pods` map (`map[PodIdentifier]*Pod`) in [client.go](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/processor/k8sattributesprocessor/internal/kube/client.go) never reclaims memory from deleted entries. This is a known Go limitation ([golang/go#20135](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/20135)): `delete()` zeroes bucket slots but never frees the bucket array. With continuous pod churn, the array only grows.

Three things interact to cause this:

1. **Map buckets never shrink (primary).** Each pod creates up to 4 entries in `c.Pods`. The `deleteLoop` removes them after 120s, but Go keeps all old bucket memory.

2. **Label cloning churn.** With `key_regex: (.*)`, every update event calls `maps.Clone` on all labels/annotations and builds a new `map[string]string` via `extractPodAttributes`.

3. **5-minute resync storms.** The hard-coded `watchSyncPeriod = 5 * time.Minute` in [informer.go](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/processor/k8sattributesprocessor/internal/kube/informer.go) fires a synthetic update for every watched pod (~92k events every 5 minutes) amplifying the above

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy the collector in a cluster with high pod churn (>1000 pod creates/deletes per hour)
2. Configure `k8sattributes` with `key_regex: (.*)` and no namespace/label filters
3. Monitor `otelcol_process_runtime_heap_alloc_bytes` over 24–48 hours
4. Capture two pprof heap profiles 10+ hours apart and diff them

## Expected Result

Memory usage should stabilize once the pod table size stabilizes. Deleted pod entries should be fully reclaimed.

## Actual Result

- `otelcol_process_runtime_heap_alloc_bytes` grows from ~500 MB to ~1.5 GB over 2.5 days (live objects)
- `otelcol_process_memory_rss` grows linearly ~600 MB/day across all replicas; one pod OOM-killed at 4.84 GB
- `otelcol_otelsvc_k8s_pod_table_size` stays stable at ~92k — the cache isn't growing, the map backing it is
- 10-hour pprof diff shows `HeapInuse` +300 MB while `inuse_space` *shrank* -44 MB — bucket retention, not an object leak

**Impact:** OOM kills observed in a test environment (pod hit 4.84 GB, restarted). Each restart forces a full API server re-list of ~92k pods before the processor can enrich data (`wait_for_metadata: true`). Each replica independently watches all pods, so all replicas grow identically — horizontal scaling does not mitigate this.

## Collector version

v0.146.0

## Environment

OS: Amazon Linux 2 (EKS -  high pod/node churn)

Test environment: 40-replica StatefulSet, 5 GiB memory limit, 4 CPU limit, ~92k watched pods

## OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

````yaml
processors:
  k8sattributes:
    wait_for_metadata: true
    wait_for_metadata_timeout: "30s"
    auth_type: "serviceAccount"
    extract:
      labels:
        - key_regex: "(.*)"
          tag_name: "pod_labels_$1"
          from: pod
        - key_regex: "(.*)"
          tag_name: "node_labels_$1"
          from: node
      metadata:
        - k8s.pod.name
        - k8s.pod.uid
        - k8s.pod.start_time
        - k8s.deployment.name
        - k8s.daemonset.name
        - k8s.replicaset.name
        - k8s.statefulset.name
        - k8s.namespace.name
        - k8s.node.name
      deployment_name_from_replicaset: true
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
      - sources:
        - from: resource_attribute
          name: k8s.pod.name
        - from: resource_attribute
          name: k8s.namespace.name

  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 90
    spike_limit_percentage: 20

extensions:
  file_storage:
    directory: /var/lib/storage/otc

# 3 exporters with persistent queue (queue_size: 50000, on_rebound: true)
````

## Log output

```
Diagnosed via pprof:

# Baseline (T=0)
HeapInuse: 1450 MB
HeapAlloc: 1023 MB

# After 10 hours (T+10h)
HeapInuse: 1750 MB (+300 MB)
HeapAlloc: 979 MB (-44 MB)

# pprof diff (inuse_space):
-44 MB total (live objects shrank, but HeapInuse grew)
```

## Additional context

**Proposed fix:** Periodically rebuild the map in `deleteLoop` to release stale buckets:

```go
func (c *WatchClient) compactPodMap() {
    newMap := make(map[PodIdentifier]*Pod, len(c.Pods))
    for k, v := range c.Pods {
        newMap[k] = v
    }
    c.Pods = newMap
}
```

**Workarounds:**
- `GOMEMLIMIT` at ~70% of container limit — slows RSS growth via more aggressive scavenging
- `deployment_name_from_replicaset: true` — eliminates Deployment/ReplicaSet informers
- Narrow `key_regex` / add namespace filters — reduces allocation churn and map size

**Related Issues:**
- #36234 — shared K8s resource caches (different root cause)
- #23067 — excessive heap after 0.78.0 (closed as stale)
- #44708 — disable deployment/replicaset informers (partially addressed by `deployment_name_from_replicaset`)

items.title: only advance file offset/checkpoint if logs are successfully processed
items.body:
### Component(s)

pkg/stanza

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When running a daemonset of collectors to tail logs, its common to:
- use the filelog reciever's checkpointing, so that if you restart an agent it picks up where it left off
- use a sending queue on your exporter, to ensure data is delivered upstream

The problem with this setup is unless you have a persistent sending queue (to disk) then your file offsets are advanced as soon as logs are emitted from the reader. If you do use a persistent sending queue, then you're duplicating reads & writes

### Describe the solution you'd like

It would be ideal if it was possible to wait to advance the filelog receiver's checkpoint until the logs have been exported, or at least implement a mechanism which checks for specific errors before advancing the offset (for example if logs are later rejected by a full sending queue).

### Describe alternatives you've considered

1. use a persistent sending queue on disk: this isn't great because now when you read file from disk, you need to write it back to disk in a different format in order for your delivery to be resilient. this is OK on a gateway, but having hundreds of agents reading and writing to disk is a lot of redundant IO and PVCs

### Additional context

here's where we'd need to bubble errors back to, I believe: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/pkg/stanza/fileconsumer/internal/reader/reader.go#L243-L247


### Reproducing
Below is a setup to reproduce:


otelcol-filelog.yaml
```
receivers:
  filelog:
    include:
      - /app/in.log
    storage: file_storage
    start_at: end
    fingerprint_size: 1kb
    max_log_size: 1MiB
    encoding: utf-8
    poll_interval: 200ms
    include_file_path: true
    include_file_name: true
    include_file_name_resolved: true

exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: http://collector2:4318
    tls:
      insecure: true
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 2s
      max_elapsed_time: 1m
      max_interval: 10s
    sending_queue:
      num_consumers: 6
      queue_size: 1000

extensions:
  file_storage:
    directory: /var/otelcol/storage

service:
  extensions: [file_storage]
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [filelog]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
```


otelcol-receiver.yaml
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

exporters:
  file:
    path: /app/out.log
    format: json

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [file]
```


then run the stack
```
docker network create otel
docker run -d \
	--name collector2 \
	--network otel \
	-v $(PWD)/otelcol-receiver.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro,z \
	-v $(PWD)/out.log:/app/out.log:rw,Z \
	otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest \
	--config /etc/otelcol/config.yaml
docker run -d \
	--name collector1 \
	--network otel \
	-v $(PWD)/otelcol-filelog.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro,z \
	-v $(PWD)/in.log:/app/in.log:ro,z \
	-v $(PWD)/storage:/var/otelcol/storage:rw,Z \
	otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest \
	--config /etc/otelcol/config.yaml```


then you can 
1. echo "123" >> in.log
2. observe the offsets in storage/receiver_filelog_ advance as expected
3. docker stop collector2
4. echo "456" >> in.log
5. observe the offsets are increased before the logs are delivered to upstream

items.title: [exporter/loadbalancing] Data loss still unavoidable under high load and autoscaling
items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/loadbalancing

### What happened?

## Description

We had the previous issue: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/35378 

However this is unfortunately not quite solved.

There is the top-level exporter queue and the sub exporter queues. To avoid data loss on an autoscale down event, there can't be queues on the sub-exporter. However if you disable this queue, it's extremely slow because the endpoints are exported to synchronously in-series. 

So, basically, if we have a queue, we get data loss on scaling. If we don't have a queue, we get data loss from performance issues because it's too slow to export. This problem gets worse the more downstream you have.

I've annotated the problematic code here with comments: 

```go
for exp, td := range exporterSegregatedTraces {
  start := time.Now()
  // with no queue, this blocks.
  // with queue, this doesn't block but causes data loss when the downstream gets scaled down.
  err := exp.ConsumeTraces(ctx, td) 
  exp.consumeWG.Done()
  errs = multierr.Append(errs, err)
  ...
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

Disable sub-exporter queue.
```yaml
  loadbalancing:
    # top-level exporter queue
    sending_queue:
      queue_size: 6000
      num_consumers: 200 # even with high consumer amount the problem persisted for us
    protocol:
      otlp:
        sending_queue:
          enabled: false
```

Then throw some load at the collector. 

Result is severe performance issues and high export times.

## Proposed solution

I think we need to have a way of disabling the sub exporter queue without blocking in series here. An `errgroup` or similar so the consumers can export to different endpoints in-parallel without relying on the sub exporter queue. Open to other ideas to solve the problem, but this seems simplest to me.


### Collector version

v0.115.0

items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/awss3exporter

### What happened?

## Description

While testing the S3 exporter's queue and retry configuration, I found that timeout errors do not result in retry.

```json

}
```

The collector does not continue to log failed requests. If I restart the collector, the failed batch is not present in the persistent sending queue. 

## Steps to Reproduce

I configured retry and sending queue. `retry_max_attempts: 100` to ensure requests retry until they are successful. I fed the pipeline a log batch of 500,000 logs. This will generally result in a timeout to s3, when using a very short timeout such as 1 second.

```yaml

    awss3/jsirianni:
        marshaler: otlp_json
        resource_attrs_to_s3:
            s3_prefix: com.awss3.prefix
        s3uploader:
            file_prefix: null
            region: us-east-2
            retry_max_attempts: 100
            retry_max_backoff: 2s
            retry_mode: standard
            s3_bucket: jsirianni-output
            s3_partition_format: year=%Y/month=%m/day=%d/hour=%H/minute=%M
            s3_prefix: drop-logs-test
        sending_queue:
            block_on_overflow: false
            enabled: true
            num_consumers: 10
            queue_size: 200
            storage: file_storage/jsirianni
            wait_for_result: false
        timeout: 1s
extensions:
    file_storage/jsirianni:
        compaction:
            directory: /opt/otel/storage
            on_rebound: true
        directory: /opt/otel/storage
```

## Expected Result

I would expect the following:
1. I should continue to see timeout errors, proving the request is retried up until the max attempts
2. When restarting the collector during the retry logic, I would expect the batch to be persisted in the queue

## Actual Result

Failed requests due to timeout are not retried. The request is not persisted in the queue. The queue appears to function if I keep feeding the exporter.

items.title: otelcol-contrib file_storage does not recover gracefully upon potentially corrupted database
items.body:
### Component(s)

extension/storage/filestorage

### What happened?

## Description
When there are issues with underlying a linux guest storage, mostly in scenarios where the hypervisor loses connectivity or experiences extremely high latency with the NAS/SAN, the database can be in a corrupted state, which requires completely deleting the filesstorage queue, to allow otel to function (or even start running) again.

## Steps to Reproduce
While a VM is running, try to remove it's storage beneath it, potentially in the middle of otel writing to the bolt filestorage. 

This may also be caused by machines being improperly shut down (like power loss.)

## Expected Result
Some data will be lost, but the filestorage extension will recover gracefully and be able to resume running.

## Actual Result
The otelcol service attempts to start, but fails to do so when loading the filestorage extension. This requires manual intervention to delete the specific filestorage file that was corrupted, and then to start the service.

### Collector version

0.106.1

### Environment information

## Environment
OS: Ubuntu 22.04
Compiler(if manually compiled): N/A, using https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/download/v0.106.1/otelcol-contrib_0.106.1_linux_amd64.deb

items.title: [kafkareceiver] The exporterhelper.ErrQueueIsFull error must enforce a backoff mechanism
items.body:
### Component(s)

receiver/kafka

### Describe the issue you're reporting

In the current implementation, the BackOff mechanism is trigerred only by [memory limiter error](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/receiver/kafkareceiver/kafka_receiver.go#L562-L564). However, the same behavior is expected for the `exporterhelper.ErrQueueIsFull` error, which occurs when there is a sending queue overflow (both [memory queue](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queuebatch/memory_queue.go#L109-L112) and [persistent queue](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queuebatch/persistent_queue.go#L244-L247)).

items.title: OTLP exporter emits empty messages when using redis storage for persistent queue
items.body: ### Component(s) extension/storage/redisstorage ### What happened? ## Description Empty otlp messages are emitted when the otlp exporter is configured with the sending queue enabled and the redis storage extension used for persistence. The same pipeline works as expected with the file storage extension. Monitoring the redis database shows that the indexes and messages are being set and retrieved from redis and the values look correct. There are no errors being reported in the collector logs. Performing a packet capture of the redis requests also shows what looks to be the expected sets, gets and responses. The body of the POST from the exporter is completely empty. ## Steps to Reproduce - configure an otel collector with an otlp receiver, otlp exporter pipeline - enable the sending queue on the exporter with file storage enabled to start to verify the pipeline - send sample telemetry to the collector and monitor the output of the otlp exporter - in my case I used another collector to receive the data as well as wireshark to view the actual otlphttp request directly - spin up a redis database if one does not already exist - in my case I used docker and the redis-stack which includes redis insight to easily monitor the database - add the redis storage extension to the collector config and reconfigure the exporter to use redis for storage - send sample telemetry to the collector and monitor the output of the otlp exporter - the messages being emitted are empty - disable the downstream otlp collection so that messages will remain in the queue - send sample telemetry to the collector and view the keys in the redis database - redis insight supports decoding the value of the key as protobuf, so you can easily read the message and see it is still intact - re-enable the downstream otlp collection and view the keys in the redis database - note the queue is cleared and the indexes are updated, indicating thing seem to be working however, the messages will still be empty ## Expected Result The messages emitted when using the redis storage extension should be intact and no different than those emitted when the file storage extension is used for the exporter persistent queue. ## Actual Result The messages are empty. ### Collector version Collector Contrib v0.118.0 ### Environment information ## Environment mac OS 14.6.1, M3 Docker Desktop 4.36.0 Redis 7.4.2 from https://hub.docker.com/r/redis/redis-stack (sha256:5b9c55e53a8b74decc26010abc6baaea632e678a07ee5fcb6ff798465ebb00b1) docker-compase.yml: ``` version: "2" services: otel-collector: image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest restart: always command: ["--config=/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml", "${OTELCOL_ARGS}"] volumes: - ./otel-collector-config.yaml:/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml - ./storage:/storage ports: - "4317:4317" # OTLP gRPC receiver - "4318:4318" # OTLP gRPC receiver ``` ### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration ```yaml receivers: otlp/telemgen: protocols: grpc: endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317 http: endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 processors: exporters: otlphttp: endpoint: http://host.docker.internal:4418 retry_on_failure: enabled: true initial_interval: 5s max_elapsed_time: 300s max_interval: 30s sending_queue: enabled: true num_consumers: 10 queue_size: 5000 storage: redis_storage timeout: 5s extensions: file_storage: directory: /storage redis_storage: db: 0 endpoint: host.docker.internal:6379 expiration: 5m password: "" service: extensions: - file_storage - redis_storage pipelines: logs: receivers: - otlp/telemgen processors: exporters: - otlphttp telemetry: logs: level: debug ``` ### Log output ```shell Output from Wireshark Follow HTTP Stream: POST /v1/logs HTTP/1.1 Host: host.docker.internal:4318 User-Agent: OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib/0.118.0 (linux/arm64) Content-Length: 23 Content-Encoding: gzip Content-Type: application/x-protobuf Accept-Encoding: gzip HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/x-protobuf Date: Sun, 02 Feb 2025 16:29:28 GMT Content-Length: 2 . ``` ### Additional context

items.title: Add alternative prometheus remote write implementation to `prometheuesremotewriteexporter`
items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/prometheusremotewrite

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

For Grafana Alloy I have been working on an alternative approach to the prometheus remote write WAL. 

### Describe the solution you'd like

Would it be reasonable to add the this new remote implementation into `prometheusremotewriteexporter`, the config options would be significantly different. Than the current WAL config so would need to only declare one or the other. Its currently experimental in Alloy but we have been using it internally and alongside several other users.

We haven't had any issues scaling it to a few million series writes a second, also looking into support for the new RW format that would mean only updating the library along with general support.

The underlying code can be found at https://github.com/grafana/walqueue

### Describe alternatives you've considered

items.title: Simplifying stateful behavior

labels.name: never stale
labels.description: Issues marked with this label will be never staled and automatically removed

items.body:
### Component(s)

extension/storage, extension/storage/filestorage, receiver/filelog

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, the collector operates in a stateless mode by default, with stateful components storing offsets in memory. However, stateful components should persist their state during shutdown if a storage extension is available.

At present, enabling stateful behavior involves a somewhat lengthy process:
1. Adding a `filestorage` entry to the `extensions` stanza in the configuration.
2. Including `filestorage` under `service::extensions`.
3. Ensuring that the storage directory exists.
4. Adding `storage: file_storage/xyz` to individual components.

It would be beneficial to simplify this process by introducing a feature gate or a single configuration option. With this approach, users could enable stateful mode with a single setting, and the necessary steps would be handled automatically, achieving the same effect as the manual steps described.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Here’s one way to tackle the enhancement:
- Introduce a new configuration provider that provides us with a default `filestorage` extension.
  - We might also consider including some commonly used extensions, such as `healtcheck`, `pprof`, `memorylimitter`, etc.
- Inject this new configuration.
- Enable stateful receivers to automatically utilize the storage extension when the feature flag is turned on.

This is a high-level overview, and I expect it will require multiple pull requests to implement.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Please share if you have any thoughts!


### Additional context

My solution would require https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/11046 to be merged or a similar workaround to be implemented to combine lists in config.

items.title: File Log receiver loses logs even if persistence is set up

labels.name: release:required-for-ga
labels.description: Must be resolved before GA release

items.body:
### Component(s)

extension/storage/filestorage, receiver/filelog

### What happened?

## Description
UPDATE: filelog receiver might be the culprit: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/31074#issuecomment-1932137539
I tried the [fault tolerant log collection example](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/examples/fault-tolerant-logs-collection), but it seemingly loses logs (does not matter if the exporter is `file` or `OTLP(GRPC)`).
`file_storage` is enabled for receiver (and for the `OTLP` exporter as well), so the state should not be lost.
I tried the `fileexporter` and the logs are lost here as well, below are the results.
## Steps to Reproduce
See gist for files: https://gist.github.com/OverOrion/2086516236e343ae2c362557302c70ce

```bash
$ cat input_gen.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash

for i in $(seq 1 600000); do
  echo line$i
done
```

### Steps:
1. Generate a big enough input file for the collector to read:
```bash
./input_gen.sh > input.log
```
2. Start the collector with the given configuration file (make sure the file receiver path points to `input.log`)
```
./otelcontribcol_linux_amd64 --config ./sender.yaml
```
3. Watch the received logs (written by the `exporter/file`) with:
```
 watch -n 1 -d "cat sender_output.log | grep -E 'line[0-9]+' -o -w | wc -l"
```
4. After some time stop the controller by pressing CTRL+C (sending a SIGINT)
5. Restart the controller using the same configuration file
6. Wait for it to finalize sending the logs and check the `sender_output.log` file:
```
cat sender_output.log | grep -E 'line[0-9]+' -o -w | wc -l
598887
```

## Expected Result
All logs should be written, no logs should be lost.

## Actual Result
In my case I consistently lose 1k+ logs out of 600k.

### Collector version

8ae1539c84a55140075063d27e62eb561f9b5dab

### Environment information

## Environment
OS: Ubuntu 23.10
Compiler(if manually compiled): go1.21.6 linux/amd64


### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

```yaml
extensions:
  file_storage/default:
    directory: /home/orion/work/others/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/persist_dir/receivers
    fsync: true

receivers:
  filelog:
    include: ["/home/orion/work/others/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/bin/input.log"]
    storage: file_storage/default
    start_at: beginning
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true

exporters:
  # Optional debug output
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed
  otlp/debug:
    endpoint: localhost:4317
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
    sending_queue:
      queue_size: 10000
    tls:

items.title: Collector fails to restart with persistent queue and health check enabled
Implement a Persistent Buffer in OpenTelemetry Collector to Prevent Data Loss
items.body:
### Component(s)

A persistent buffer

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The Otel collector normally operates as a stateless pipeline. Due to the statelessness, data can be dropped at any point in the pipeline if an error is encountered. It is possible to set up retries and the exporter helper's retry queue, but the sending queue is asynchronous as the operation is fire-and-forget. I'd like a better handle around which data is actually sent from component to component in the pipeline so I am assured that nothing is dropped.

### Describe the solution you'd like

To be able to manage state I'd like a new processing or consumer component that integrates a persistent buffer layer (i.e. some key-value store). This buffer will precede each defined Otel consumer (processors or exporters) to ensure data can be passed from one component to another without issues. In the case of errors, the component that failed can be identified, and retries can be performed within set thresholds. This configuration introduces state management to the Otel pipeline, which is typically stateless, enhancing data reliability and minimizing the risk of data loss.

**The following outlines a ConsumeLogs call in the buffer processor, as an example:**

The incoming plog.Logs are iterated over first by the resource logs, then by the scope logs and finally by the logs where the log body data is persisted. The call to persist the data needs to be as robust as possible with its own retry mechanism in the event of any failure. Once the call to persist the data succeeds, it is possible to push the logs to the next consumer. The error case is covered below.

**Calling the next processor:**

In the persist buffer processor, if the nextConsumer is not nil, then proceed to send the logs.

**In the event of a failure after calling the next processor:**

If a failure is encountered while sending the logs, the buffer consumer should attempt to retry sending the logs within some configured threshold. If the threshold is exceeded, depending upon the desired configuration, the pipeline can either enter a terminal state or continue on to the next component for processing.

**Collector shutdown:**

Upon collector shutdown, data will remain in the persistent buffer. The next section (collector startup/restart) helps define if the data persisted will be sent further along in the collector or not.

**Collector startup/restart:**

When the collector is started or restarted, the persistent buffer can check if there is data still present. If so, similar to the [OTLP protocol](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/protocol/otlp.md#duplicate-data), duplicate data will be sent. Otherwise if data failed to send before due to the machine powering down, or the process crashing, the data is retrieved from the buffer and sent along for the first time. There would need to be some sort of identifier that the buffer processor can use so it knows if it should be sending the data that is present in the buffer or if it should discard it given that the pipeline changed or was re-configured and the old data is stale.

**Persistent buffer data removal:**

Data doesn't stay in the persistent buffer forever. When the call to the nextConsumer is successful, the data added to the buffer is removed. To avoid stale data and causing the buffer to grow too large, a TTL can also be configured. 

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I've investigated the following alternatives:

- Relying on the exporter helper's retry queue: This a great feature to have, but I want to have more control over knowing if data was retried successfully. The current retry mechanism is essentially fire-and-forget and if the retry doesn't end up succeeding after the allowed number of retries, the data is lost.
- Callbacks: there is a possibility that callbacks could work in some Otel scenarios; however, things get complicated when using batch processors that are able to slice the logs, metrics, or traces based on a threshold of allowed data to be sent per batch. The callback story gets too complicated because an incoming callback gets split into how many returning callbacks?

### Additional context

I am currently working on this, and welcome any feedback. Thank you!

items.title: [exporter/elasticsearch] Data should not be dropped with persistent queue enabled when ES cluster is temporarily unavailable
items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/elasticsearch

### What happened?

## Description

If the Elasticsearch exporter is configured with a persistent queue (`sending_queue.storage: filestorage`) and new data is written to this persistent queue while the Elasticsearch cluster is temporarily unavailable, this data should be indexed into Elasticsearch once the cluster becomes available again.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the collector like so:
   ```yaml
   receivers:
     filelog:
       include: /tmp/*.log
       storage: file_storage/filelogreceiver

   exporters:
     elasticsearch:
       endpoints: [ "http://localhost:9200" ]
       index: foo
       flush:
         interval: 1s
       sending_queue:
         enabled: true
         storage: file_storage/elasticsearchexporter

   extensions:
     file_storage/filelogreceiver:
       directory: /tmp/otelcol/file_storage/filelogreceiver
     file_storage/elasticsearchexporter:
       directory: /tmp/otelcol/file_storage/elasticsearchexporter
    
   service:
     extensions: [file_storage/filelogreceiver, file_storage/elasticsearchexporter]
     pipelines:
       logs:
         receivers: [filelog]
         exporters: [elasticsearch]
     telemetry:
       logs:
         level: debug
     ```
2. Start the collector.
3. Add a log entry to the file.
   ```shell
   echo "1 foo bar $RANDOM" >> /tmp/test.log
   ```
4. Query the Elasticsearch cluster to verify that the log entry made it into the index.
5. Stop the Elasticsearch cluster.
6. Add a new log entry to the file.
   ```shell
   echo "2 foo bar $RANDOM" >> /tmp/test.log
   ```
7. Restart the Elasticsearch cluster.
8. Query the Elasticsearch cluster to verify that the second log entry made it into the index.

## Expected Result

* In step 8, there should be two log entries in the index.

## Actual Result

* In step 8, only the first log entry (added in step 3) is in the index.


### Collector version

v0.93.0

### Environment information

## Environment
OS: (e.g., "Ubuntu 20.04") MacOS
Compiler(if manually compiled): (e.g., "go 14.2") go 1.21.6


### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

```yaml
receivers:
  filelog:
    include: /tmp/*.log
    storage: file_storage/filelogreceiver

exporters:
  elasticsearch:
    endpoints: [ "http://localhost:9200" ]
    index: foo
    flush:
      interval: 1s
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      storage: file_storage/elasticsearchexporter

extensions:
  file_storage/filelogreceiver:
    directory: /tmp/otelcol/file_storage/filelogreceiver
  file_storage/elasticsearchexporter:
    directory: /tmp/otelcol/file_storage/elasticsearchexporter
    
service:
  extensions: [file_storage/filelogreceiver, file_storage/elasticsearchexporter]
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [filelog]
      exporters: [elasticsearch]
  telemetry:
    logs:
      level: debug
```

items.title: Support external queue system for exporter via extensions
items.body:
### Component(s)

_No response_

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

No

### Describe the solution you'd like

I want the ability to utilize Redis as the exporter queue to support upstream outages for longer period. The current two options of exporter do not fulfill the requirements or have issues with longer outages.

This usecase came up because I needed near 0% data loss on logs over long periods of time because the upstream is known to be down for many mins. The in-memory queue was ruled out because it would lose data on pod restarts. The persistent queue option was promising but it started refusing new data if the queue is full and based on the code it is difficult to disable the refusal which causes loss of new data once the queue is full.

So since I had access to a Redis cluster, I decided to modify the exporter to support Redis as the queue. I was able to test this and get stable data flow, however I was not able to do proper and long testing yet.

Can this feature be implemented via extensions so in future other queue systems could be added as well? I believe the existing queue systems will need to moved to extensions in that case. 

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Alternatives considered
- In-memory Queue: As mentioned, data is lost if the pod restarts due to crashes.
- Persistent Queue: Starts refusing new data when the queue is full.
- Export to Pulsar, receive from Pulsar: This does work, but the 2nd collector still needs one of the above queue during exporting, ending up in same situation.

### Additional context

Config example
```yaml
exporters:
  logging:
  otlp:
    endpoint: "localhost:4217"
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 5s
      max_interval: 5s
      max_elapsed_time: 20s
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      requeue_enabled: true
      queue_backend: redis
      num_consumers: 10
      queue_size: 10000
      redis:
        address: "localhost:6379"
        backlog_check_interval: 30
        process_key_expiration: 120
        scan_key_size: 10
    tls:
      insecure: true
```
While queue_size is mentioned 10000, it is actually unlimited because redis can scale up based on usage.

items.title: Consider testing enhancements for `filelog` receiver
items.body:
### Component(s)

receiver/filelog

### Describe the issue you're reporting

As of today the OTel Collector can handle log collection without loss or duplication after restarts.
This is possible by using the [storage extension](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/extension/storage/filestorage) to store the receiver's state and using a [persistent-queue](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/README.md#persistent-queue) to persist the exporter's state.
This is documented at the [offset tracking](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/receiver/filelogreceiver/README.md#offset-tracking) section and the [fault-tolerant-logs-collection](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/examples/fault-tolerant-logs-collection/README.md) example.

However there are cases where it has been reported data loss like at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/31074, in which is not quite straightforward from where the issue comes from. This also indicates the lack of e2e testing for this important use case.

It is already mentioned the need for e2e tests at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/20552 however since that issue is more generic I would like to propose a more specific scope here to cover use cases like https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/31074.

In this regard, we should consider implementing e2e tests for at least the following scenarios:

### A) Basic restart scenarios (offset tracking)

1. The collector must track file offsets, even after a restart and continue where it left off without any data loss or data duplication
2. The collector must ship logs (only once) when the backend is temporarily unavailable even if Collector restarts occur during the "backend outage" 

### B) Nice to have(s):

1. We should be able to update/downgrade/re-install without losing the offset data
2. We should correctly track offsets even in the case of a hard crash

### C) Changes on target files

1. We should be able to rotate files with move-create strategy without losing or duplicating data
2. We should be able to rotate files with copy-truncate strategy without losing or duplicating data
3. We should be able to read a file to the end even after it's deleted
4. We should be able to keep reading from a file even after it's moved (e.g: foo.log -> foo.log.1) and there should not be duplicate entries from the moved file (which could be caused due to erroneously re-reading it from the beginning)

items.title: Support k8s log file in syslog exporter
items.body:
### Component(s)

exporter/syslog

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

We want to collect k8s logs through openTelemetry Collector, and then analyze the logs outside. The initial idea is to setup syslog server and forward logs to HDFS cluster. The openTelemetry Collector helps to forward k8s logs to syslog server. 

I create a pipeline with filelog receiver and syslog exporter. But failed to receive any UDP package in external syslog server. It sounds the k8s log is not syslog format then syslog exporter didn't do anything.
I didn't find any syslog processor or formatter in pipeline techs.

```
    exporters:
      syslog:
        endpoint: 23.21.46.218
        network: udp
        port: 5140
        protocol: rfc5424
        retry_on_failure:
          enabled: true
          initial_interval: 10s
          max_elapsed_time: 150s
          max_interval: 40s
        sending_queue:
          enabled: true
          num_consumers: 20
          queue_size: 10000
        timeout: 1s
    receivers:
      filelog:
        exclude: []
        include:
        - /var/log/pods/*/*/*.log
        include_file_name: false
        include_file_path: true
    service:
      extensions: {}
      pipelines:
        logs:
          exporters:
          - syslog
          receivers:
          - filelog
 ```
Any suggestion?

### Describe the solution you'd like

Is it possible to create sylog processor like this;
```
processors:
  syslog:
    input_format: "json"
    output_format: "rfc5424"
    rfc5424:
      app_name: "my-app"
      facility: "local0"
```

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

items.title: Add end-to-end tests to verify no data loss in stressed situations

labels.name: never stale
labels.description: Issues marked with this label will be never staled and automatically removed

items.body:
### Problem

I have [been recently looking](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7460) at how the Collector behaves in stressed situations (e.g. when memory limiter kicks in) and found that we have a number of places on our codebase where the components don't behave according to the contract and that results in data losses.

While it is important to test individual components to make sure they work as expected I think it is also necessary to have end-to-end tests that verify the behavior of the Collector as a whole since it is hard to guarantee that the combination of the components works as expected just by looking at the individual component unit tests.

### Proposed Solution

I would like to add a new end-to-end integration test:

- Use the existing [testbed](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/testbed).
- Run Collector [in-process](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/testbed/testbed/in_process_collector.go) for shorter test durations.
- Component sets to verify:
  - Receivers: `otlp` (grpc and http transports), `filelog`, `prometheus`
  - Processors: `memorylimiter` alone AND `memorylimiter`->`batchprocessor` combination
  - Exporters `otlp`, `otlphttp`.
- Scenarios to verify:
  - Memory [limit](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/b2961b799e2c1ec128f0539764af1fa10c839e04/processor/memorylimiterprocessor/config.go#L34) is hit, then recovered.
  - Exporter helper QueuedRetry [queue limit size](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/b2961b799e2c1ec128f0539764af1fa10c839e04/exporter/exporterhelper/queued_retry.go#L50) is hit.
  - Input rate (receiving) exceeds output rate (exporting) temporarily, long enough to cause hitting the above limits.
  - Destination is unavailable, then becomes available.
  - Exporter is sporadically available (return errors randomly).
  - QueuedRetry with in-memory AND [persistent](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/b2961b799e2c1ec128f0539764af1fa10c839e04/exporter/exporterhelper/queued_retry.go#L53) queue options.
  - QueuedRetry with queuing [disabled](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/b2961b799e2c1ec128f0539764af1fa10c839e04/exporter/exporterhelper/queued_retry.go#L46).

Because the number of possible combination to test can be very large we may want to reduce them using pairwise combinatorial testing (already used by correctness tests) instead of full matrix testing.

What to verify:
- No data is lost
- No data is duplicated

## Test Data Senders and Receivers

This test will require generators that can send data to the Collector and data receivers that can accept the data and simulate success/failure for every protocol that we want to test. 

We already such [data senders](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/testbed/datasenders) and [data receivers](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/testbed/datareceivers) for load generation purposes. It is highly advisable into the possibility to reuse these (if necessary extend them to support the scenarios we want to test for).

### Alternatives Considered

Unit testing only. I don't think this is good enough, we have way to many moving parts in different components and different ways to connect them to be confident based on just unit testing.

items.title: [extensions/file_storage] Change bbolt settings for better performance on large DB files
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
File storage performance degrades significantly depending on the maximum size of the bbolt DB over its lifetime. Notably, this is true even if the DB is empty, as bbolt never frees disk space unless manually instructed to compact it (which is tricky to do online). The reason for the performance degradation is that bbolt keeps a freelist data structure to track storage space, and the default implementation of this structure is prone to fragmentation. In the default configuration, it also syncs this freelist to disk on every transaction, which can be expensive if it's large. 

See the additional context section for benchmarks.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. Disable freelist syncing for bbolt. This increases startup time by two orders of magnitude (~2 ms -> ~200ms for a 2 GB db file), but makes every operation close to 2x faster. See benchmarks below and the [bbolt documentation](https://pkg.go.dev/go.etcd.io/bbolt#Options.NoFreelistSync) for reference.
2. Switch to a different freelist data structure. This makes small dbs around 10% slower, but larger ones many orders of magnitude faster. See the [bbolt documentation for freelist types](https://pkg.go.dev/go.etcd.io/bbolt#Options.FreelistType) for reference.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Compaction solves this problem, but requires manually enabling it and restarting the application. It also requires additional disk space and increases start time much in the same way as not syncing the freelist does.

This is a problem we've originally discovered in core's persistent queue. It can also be mitigated there by explicitly rotating DB files. This is fairly complex though, and the options changes look like a performance win for everyone with little downside.

**Additional context**
I've added two additional benchmarks to the existing suite.
`BenchmarkClientSetLargeDB` does the same benchmark as `BenchmarkClientSet`, but it prepares the DB by inserting 2000 1Mi values, and then deleting them. `BenchmarkClientInitLargeDB` does the same preparation, and then reopens the DB, forcing it to regenerate the freelist. I'm going to submit a PR with these shortly.
